title: MeshMend: STL Repair

candidates.name: MeshMend: STL Repair
candidates.why: The ownable carrier is paired with the two-word job phrase observed in STL-repair searches; it names file repair rather than generic model viewing.

candidates.name: STL Repair
candidates.why: It says the searched job plainly, but the generic phrase is difficult to own and does not distinguish a changed-file pipeline from simple repair.

candidates.name: MeshMend
candidates.why: The short coined carrier is memorable but omits the STL repair job words and depends on users already knowing the brand.

candidates.name: BedReady
candidates.why: It hints at a printable result but does not tell a user that the app repairs an existing mesh file.

candidates.name: FileForge
candidates.why: It suggests file transformation but is broad enough to describe unrelated file tools and lacks the model-repair query.

rejected.name: STL Viewer
rejected.reason: The broad result shelf already contains multiple STL Viewer titles, and viewing alone is the incomplete job this proposal adds repair and print-risk checks to.

rejected.name: 3D Print Prep
rejected.reason: The phrase describes a broad category rather than the distinctive changed-mesh repair action, and it risks looking interchangeable with printer companion tools.

audience: A 3D-print hobbyist with an existing STL or 3MF model who wants to repair its geometry and check likely print risks on a phone before sending it to a slicer.
rationale: The title scans measured weak Android results around STL viewing and phone slicing, while sampled users complain about dark rendering, file access, and paywalls for viewing; the title therefore names a repair job rather than copying a viewer title, but the brand is not legally cleared.
collisionCheck: The 2026-10-08 scan-titles command searched MeshMend STL Repair and MeshMend. No exact MeshMend: STL Repair title appeared in the visible cards, but the standalone MeshMend query returned 12 mostly unrelated cards with a polluted relevance guard; Google Play title search is not trademark clearance, and no USPTO, EUIPO, WIPO, or Russian register was queried.
localisationCheck: The proposed English and Russian titles are each 20 characters, both below Play's 30-character cap; the short Latin carrier is retained while the Russian job words are localized, and the Cyrillic phrasing still needs native-speaker review.

scoringRubric.floor: chosen >= 70 with no dimension below 2.5; a hard check outranks the score

assumptionsUnverified: UNVERIFIED: no trademark register was queried, so MeshMend's availability in downloadable software class 9 is not known.
UNVERIFIED: Google Play search does not establish that the title is unique across all localized or unpublished listings.
UNVERIFIED: the Russian localized job phrase needs a native-speaker and searchability review.
